title: Button hierarchy: primary, secondary, tertiary
when: The user wants consistent button styles, or a screen has several actions competing for attention.
prompt:
Goal: Three or four button levels with one primary per view, shared sizing, and hover, active, focus, disabled and busy states.
Steps:
1. Levels: primary (solid accent), secondary (outline or tint), tertiary (text, underlined), destructive (solid danger, to confirm only).
2. Allow one primary per view or dialog; demote the rest.
3. Base .btn: inline-flex with gap for an icon, min-height: 44px, padding-inline: var(--space-4), font-weight: 600, radius from the scale.
4. States: :hover one ramp step darker, :active one more, :focus-visible 2px outline with offset, [aria-disabled="true"] with lower contrast.
5. Label with verb and object (Save changes) and keep the primary in the same spot everywhere, for example last in dialog footers.
6. Use button for actions and a for navigation.
Quality bar:
- The primary is obvious in a squint test.
- Labels on solid buttons pass 4.5 to 1.
- One default size plus at most one small size.
Pitfalls:
- Two solid buttons side by side.
- Disabled buttons with no reason shown.
- Clickable divs instead of buttons.
Verify:
- [ ] A .btn base plus level modifiers.
- [ ] Each level has all states.
- [ ] Buttons state their type.
- [ ] Contrast passes.
Output: Button rules in style.css and the classes used in the pages.

examples.input: my checkout page has 4 buttons that all look the same
examples.output: Pay now primary solid, Edit cart secondary outline, Continue shopping tertiary text link
